description: Two-row composite figure comparing impact-fracture morphologies of (a) LN and (b) HN steels; each row combines three panel types at increasing magnification. Left of each row is a pseudo-colour 3D reconstruction of the fracture-surface relief, with a vertical colour bar in mm running from dark blue at 0.00 mm to red at the top value — 7.53 mm for (a) and 9.95 mm for (b); the in-plane axes carry the printed labels 0, 5.00, 10.00 and 12.50 mm in (a) and 0, 5.00, 10.00 mm in (b). Centre: a low-magnification SEM of the whole fracture surface with a 1 mm scale bar, a white polygon outlining the peripheral zone and a small black square marking the region enlarged at right. Right: high-magnification SEM of the dimpled fibrous zone with a 10 µm scale bar, showing dimples in (a) that are smaller and elongated and in (b) that are larger, deeper and more uniform. The figure is composite and makes one argument: the macro-scale fracture geometry (shear-lip outline) and the micron-scale dimple character both differ between LN and HN.
measured_quantities: fracture surface relief height (mm) from the 3D colour scale
scale-bar lengths (1 mm overview, 10 µm high magnification)
shear lip zone area ratio (stated in the citing text, no value printed on the figure)
dimple size and average depth (qualitative; no value printed on the figure)

observations.observation: The figure is a two-row composite; row (a) is labelled LN and row (b) HN, and each row contains three panels of increasing magnification (3D relief map, low-mag SEM overview, high-mag SEM).
The left panel of (a) is a pseudo-colour 3D surface-relief reconstruction with a printed mm colour scale spanning 0.00 to 7.53 mm (blue to red) and in-plane tick labels 0, 5.00, 10.00 and 12.50 mm.
The left panel of (b) is the same type of pseudo-colour 3D relief reconstruction but with a colour scale printed 0.00 to 9.95 mm and in-plane tick labels 0, 5.00 and 10.00 mm.

Both central panels are low-magnification SEM images of an entire rectangular impact-fracture surface carrying a 1 mm scale bar, a white polygon outlining the peripheral zone and a small black square marking the region magnified in the right panel.

Both right-hand panels are high-magnification SEM images with a 10 µm scale bar showing a dimpled (fibrous) fracture surface; the dimples in (a) appear smaller and more elongated while those in (b) appear larger, deeper and more uniform.
No numeric dimple sizes, depths or shear-lip area percentages are printed on any panel; the only printed numbers are the colour-bar values, the in-plane tick labels and the scale bars.
The caption states the figure shows the morphologies of impact fracture for (a) LN and (b) HN steels.
The citing text states the impact fractures of the LN and HN steel samples presented a standard ductile impact fracture comprising fibrous, radiation (radial) and shear-lip zones.

The citing text states that the area ratio of the shear-lip zone in the HN steel sample was significantly higher than in the LN steel, indicating a slower crack growth rate and better impact toughness.

The citing text states that the fracture dimples of the LN steel were elongated in the direction of crack propagation, whereas the size and average depth of the dimples of the HN steel were large and uniform.

The citing text attributes the improved impact toughness of HN steel to finer grains with more curved grain boundaries that impede crack propagation, while ferrite precipitated at the austenite grain boundaries promotes crack initiation and brittle propagation.

subfigures.description: Row for LN steel: left is a pseudo-colour 3D surface-relief reconstruction with a mm colour bar 0.00-7.53 mm and in-plane tick labels 0, 5.00, 10.00, 12.50 mm; centre is a low-magnification SEM of the full fracture surface (1 mm scale bar) with a white polygon tracing the peripheral shear-lip/outer zone and a black square ROI; right is a high-magnification SEM (10 µm scale bar) of the ROI showing small, elongated dimples.

Row for HN steel: left is the corresponding pseudo-colour 3D surface-relief reconstruction with a mm colour bar 0.00-9.95 mm and tick labels 0, 5.00, 10.00 mm; centre is the low-magnification SEM of the full fracture surface (1 mm scale bar) with white outline and black square ROI; right is the high-magnification SEM (10 µm scale bar) showing larger, deeper and more uniform dimples.

unreadable_items: The height/relief axis of the two 3D reconstruction panels (left column) is not explicitly labelled with a quantity name, and the caption does not describe these panels; their numeric significance (whether the printed values are specimen dimensions or relief depth) is therefore uncertain.
Whether the white polygon outlines the shear-lip zone specifically cannot be confirmed from the pixels alone; the caption does not mention it.
